From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helixai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T08:14:00Z
Subject: Realtime stream cutoff at 08:10 — multiple 504s and truncated chunks

Vanessa,

We started seeing production failures at ~08:10 (us-east-1). Multiple customer requests to our chat endpoint that use Redwood streaming responses are either truncating mid-chunk or returning a 504 after ~30s. When streaming works, the client sees a JSON chunk and then the socket closes without a final 'done' event. CPU and GPU on our side look fine — traffic spiked from 10 RPS to ~60 RPS within 2 minutes.

Quick details:
- Model: redwood/gptx-8k-v1 (hosted)
- Route: /v1/chat/stream (chunked transfer / websocket fallback)
- Symptoms: chunk boundary dropped, intermittent socket RST, client retries get 504s
- We've attached sample logs and a short pcap of client <-> proxy traffic.

Can your team take a look? This is impacting our SSO customers and some live demos. We need either a mitigation or a ETA for fix.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior SRE, HelixAI

Attachments: helixai_error_log_08-14.txt, pcap_stream_20270428.zip

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-28T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: ESCL: HelixAI prod stream blackout — preliminary triage

Quick status update from infra: we reproduced the symptom in a synthetic test that mimics Helix traffic shape. Observations:
- Edge proxies are emitting HTTP/1.1 chunked bodies but the NLB is closing connections with RST ~18-22s after a period of low payload (we saw chunk intervals >15s during the spike).
- Websocket fallback sessions show an immediate TCP-level reset in the same timeframe.
- The proxy's current keepalive behavior was tuned to minimize connections; under sudden spike the proxy delays flushes to batch tokens which leaves the connection idle from the NLB perspective.

Hypothesis: a timing interaction between our chunked-transfer batching/keepalive and the cloud NLB idle/reset threshold is causing mid-stream closures.

Immediate mitigations deployed at 09:02:
1) Edge proxy rollback to conservative keepalive (flush tokens every 3s).
2) Route-level emergency policy: during incident, force websocket fallback disabled and use short-chunk streaming (smaller chunks).
3) Added temporary healthcheck tweak on NLB to extend idle window for Helix routes.

Early results: error rate down ~60% for test traffic. Still monitoring production. Next: collect full NLB trace and correlate with pcap Helix provided.

-markus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: edge-proxy-dump-0810.json

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-28T15:40:00Z
Subject: RESOLVED: HelixAI streaming incident — temporary mitigation in place; post-mortem planned

Alex / Claire — final update for the day: status is RESOLVED (error-rate and 504s returned to baseline). Summary and next steps below.

Root cause (summary): interaction between our chunked-transfer batching strategy and the cloud NLB's idle/reset behavior under a sudden traffic spike. In short, our proxy aggressively batched small token flushes to optimize throughput; when token delivery intervals exceeded the NLB's perceived idle threshold, the NLB terminated the connection mid-stream.

What we deployed (timeline):
- 09:02: conservative keepalive/flush policy at edge proxy (flush <=3s).
- 09:10: temporary route policy to reduce chunk size and disable websocket fallback for impacted customers.
- 13:00: additional NLB idle-window extension applied for Helix routes.
- 14:25: rollback of websocket disable for control group after confirmation of stable behavior.

Impact: reduction of streaming 504s to baseline; no data corruption observed, some requests were retried by clients.

Permanent plan:
1) Engineering to ship a robust keepalive-aware chunking mode in the runtime that inserts a lightweight keepalive chunk (<=1 byte) when chunk intervals exceed X seconds. Target: code rollout in 2 weeks.
2) Update deployment docs and default proxy config to be conservative for customers with NLBs.
3) Post-incident review opened: JIRA INF-2198. We'll share a formal post-mortem and remediation timeline by EOW.

Attachments: pcap_stream_20270428.zip, helixai_error_log_08-14.txt, edge-proxy-dump-0810.json

Thanks for your patience and for the quick collaboration. We'll follow up with the post-mortem and confirm the smaller runtime patch schedule.

Best,
Vanessa
